description: The agent must: (1) Discover the `tweet-thread-generator.sh` script in the workspace root by reading the SKILL.md or exploring the workspace. (2) For the first invocation, use `file` as the first positional argument (source mode) and `docs/internal/briefs/devops_automation_brief.md` as the second positional argument, combined with `--tone professional` and `--topic 'DevOps Automation'` flags. Capture the full stdout into `thread_draft_professional.txt`. (3) For the second invocation, use `text` as the first positional argument and the inline blurb string as the second positional argument, with `--tone casual` and `--topic 'DevOps Automation'`. Capture full stdout into `thread_draft_casual.txt`. The proprietary trap is that the script requires the source mode (`text`, `file`, `url`, `interactive`) as a specific positional argument — not a flag — and uses `--tone` (not `--style` or `--voice`) as the tone flag. An agent guessing flags from general knowledge would likely fail the source-mode detection checks. Both output files must contain the full script output including the thread body, the markdown metrics table (`| Tweets | 3 |`, `| Engagement Rate | ~3-5% |`), the hashtag section, the tips section, and the `✅ Thread generated!` completion marker.
